category_title: Low-attaining students who remain quiet and passive during teacher-directed discussions
student_description: This student is quiet and passive, often masking their lack of engagement by appearing attentive while simply waiting for discussions to end. When they do participate, their contributions are extremely brief (often under four words), and they tend to shut down when asked open-ended follow-up questions. They uniquely require low-barrier participation methods, visual anchoring of ideas, and explicit instruction on how to be an active listener.

criteria.rationale: The student masks their disengagement by sitting quietly; they need to be explicitly taught that listening is an active, critical role, not just waiting.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes explicitly teaching the student the purpose of discussions and specific behaviors for active, critical listening.

criteria.rationale: Prolonged whole-class discussions allow this student to slip into passive attendance, so reducing discussion time in favor of targeted individual support is necessary.
criteria.check: The long-term plan involves reducing the length of whole-class discussions to maintain focus and reallocating that time toward individual scaffolding.
